title: &aArms and Armour
subtitle: Weapons, shields, trinkets, backpacks, and what happens when you fall.

quests.title: Every Weapon Has a Rhythm
quests.subtitle: Better Combat, in depth
desc: With &eBetter Combat&r each weapon type has its own combo: keep attacking to chain it. Wide swings hit everything in the arc, thrusts reach further, and the last hit of a combo is often the strongest.
Two one-handers can be dual-wielded (one in each hand). Two-handers need an empty off-hand. Use &eCombat Roll&r to dodge out of a boss's swing (search 'roll' in Controls).

quests.title: Fifteen Ways to Fight
desc: &eSimply Swords&r adds fifteen weapon types: longsword, katana, rapier, sai, cutlass, claymore, greataxe, greathammer, scythe, spear, glaive, halberd, chakram, twinblade and warglaive.
Each comes in iron, gold, diamond and netherite. Fast weapons suit hit-and-run fighters; heavy ones suit tanks and berserkers. Try a few.

quests.title: Weapons With a Name
desc: Simply Swords' &eunique weapons&r (Emberblade, Stormbringer, Soulrender, The Watcher and dozens more) can't be crafted. They come from dungeon chests and boss loot.
Each has its own power, on hit or on right-click: read the tooltip. Some take &eRunefused&r or &eNetherfused gems&r for a second power.

quests.title: Weapons From Another Game
desc: &eDungeons Weapons&r brings gear from Minecraft Dungeons: claymores, daggers, double axes, maces, sickles, anchors and great hammers.
Gold-named versions (Firebrand, Stormlander, Sun's Grace, Nightmare's Bite) are rare finds with extra powers. Keep an eye on your loot.

quests.title: The Smith's Metal
quests.subtitle: Epic Knights
desc: &eEpic Knights&r adds medieval armour, shields and weapons, and most of it starts with &eSteel&r. Look up the Steel Ingot in JEI (press &eR&r) to see how it's made.
Steel also makes plates and chain for the heavier armours.

quests.title: Full Plate
desc: Pick a harness that suits you: Gothic, Maximilian, Crusader, Winged Hussar, Kastenbrust and more. Helmets (Armet, Bascinet, Greathelm, Sallet) mix with any set.
Heavy plate is the early wall for front-line players: the Orange Hoardwarden and Green Lightwarden live in it.

quests.title: Lances and Two-Handers
desc: An Epic Knights &elance&r hits much harder from horseback: a mounted charge can break a raider line. Zweihanders, flails, pikes and halberds are slow but brutal on foot.
Optional, but a knight on a horse is a fine sight.

quests.title: A Better Guard
quests.subtitle: Shield Expansion
desc: Blocking with &eShield Expansion&r costs stamina, and a well-timed block &eparries&r. Better shields block more before they break your guard and give a wider parry window.
Shields go wood, iron, gold, diamond, netherite. Parry a boss's big swing and you get a free opening.

quests.title: Unbreakable Guard
desc: The &eNetherite Shield&r is the strongest guard in the pack. It won't burn if you drop it in lava, and it shrugs off most things short of a boss.
Tanks: pair it with heavy plate and stand in front of your party.

quests.title: Trinkets and Mimics
quests.subtitle: Artifacts
desc: &eArtifacts&r are magic trinkets (Running Shoes, Cloud in a Bottle, Feral Claws, Lucky Scarf, Night Vision Goggles...) worn in your curio slots beside the inventory.
You find them in chests and underground camps, but some chests are &cMimics&r: if a chest bites, kill it. Mimics drop an artifact.

quests.title: A Bigger Pack
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Backpacks
desc: Upgrade your backpack in a crafting table to keep its contents: leather, then copper, iron, gold, diamond and netherite. Open it with &eB&r while you wear it.
Upgrades go in its side slots: &ePickup&r and &eMagnet&r grab loot, &eFeeding&r feeds you, and &eCrafting&r, &eSmelting&r and &eTool Swapper&r do what they say.

quests.title: Deep Pockets
desc: A &eDiamond Backpack&r holds a small storage room and more upgrade slots. Add a &eMagnet Upgrade&r and loot flies to you after a fight.
Stack Upgrades let each slot hold far more than 64. Great for miners.

quests.title: When You Fall
quests.subtitle: Corpse
desc: When you die, your items stay in a &eCorpse&r where you fell, marked on your map. Right-click it to take everything back.
A corpse with items in it never despawns, never falls into the void and never burns in lava. Friends can open it too, so a party member can carry your gear home.

quests.title: Master-at-Arms
desc: A named weapon, plate on your back, a shield that won't break, and a pack full of loot. You're armed for what's coming.
From here, Apotheosis affixes, Iron's school armour and boss gear take you further.
